SAP Labs Interview Experience 2022 
Amogh Prabhu, B. Tech IT’24. 
 
Online Test: 
An online test for 45 mins was conducted on the SHL platform.  
The test had 2 simple questions. 
1. We are given a string which should contain only English alphabetical characters, 
spaces, and numbers. If the string contains some other character then we need to 
find the total occurrence of such characters. 
E.g., If the given string is “Hello World, 1 + 2 = 3” then the output will be 3 (‘,’ ,’+’, 
‘=’). 
 
I iterated through each character in the string and incremented the count when a 
character was not an English alphabetical character, space, or number. 
(Passed all test cases) 
 
2. Martin’s father goes for a jog every morning. Martin follows him several minutes 
later. His father starts at a position that is X1 meters away from their home and runs 
rectilinearly at a constant speed of V1 meters per step for N steps. 
Martin is standing at X2 meters away from his home. He wonders how fast he must 
run at some constant speed of V2 meters per step to maximize F, where F equals 
the number of his father's footsteps that Martin will land on during his run. It is 
given that the first step that Martin will land on, from his starting position, will have 
been landed on by his father. Note that if more than one prospective velocity 
results in the same number of maximum common steps, output the highest 
prospective velocity as V2. 
Calculate F and V2. 
 
E.g., Input: 
Martin’s initial position: 0 
Martin’s father’s initial position: 3 
N = 5 
V1 = 2 
So, output should be F = 2 and V2 = 7.

Explanation:  
When Martin starts walking, his dad would have walked 5 steps (5,7,9,11,13) 
starting from position 3 with speed 2m/steps.     
Since his first step should land on his father’s past steps, the possible values 
of V2 are 3,5,7,9,11,13 i.e., the total distance of the steps from Martin’s 
initial position, 
For V2 = 3,5,7 we get F = 2 and for V2 = 9,11,13 we get F = 1. 
Hence output is V2 = 7 and F = 2 (As highest value of F is 2 and for F = 2 
highest value of V2 is 7). https://brainly.in/question/43383542 
 
For all possible values of V2 I calculated the F value. 
(Passed 9/10 test cases). 
 
Technical Round 1: 
The interviewer was very nice. He asked me to introduce myself. He asked me about 
my hobbies. Then he asked me about the projects and domains that I have worked on. 
After my introduction he started with the technical questions. 
Questions I was asked – 
1. OOP 
 What is Object Oriented Programming?  
https://www.javatpoint.com/what-is-object-oriented-programming 
 Give example of an Object-Oriented Programming Language? (JAVA). 
 Is C++ an Object-Oriented Programming Language? (Partially OOPL). 
 Difference between C++ and JAVA. (He asked me about the global variables 
(Java does not have global variables)). 
 What are different types of Polymorphism?  
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/polymorphism-in-c/ 
 
2. OS 
 List the Process Scheduling Algorithms. (FIFO, SJF, Priority, Round Robin). 
 Explain working of Round Robin Scheduling Algorithm. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-round-robin-scheduling-set-1/ 
 
3. DSA 
 How much space does a class take? (Class will not occupy any space if no 
instance of that class has been created yet). 
 Is linked list a linear data structure? (Yes) 
 Longest Palindromic Substring 
Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s. 
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-palindromic-substring/

The interviewer asked me to present my screen and code in any text editor. 
I used VS code. 
 
My Solution: Expand Around Centre 
There are two cases in a palindrome: 
Case 1: Palindrome has odd length. 
In the given string find the character with maximum number of equal characters on 
both the sides. 
Example: For string “abbabbaad”, ‘a’ at index 3 has 3 equal characters on both the 
sides. Hence the centre of palindrome will be ‘a’ at index 3. (Solution will be 
s.substring(idx-length, idx+length)) 
Case 2: Palindrome has even length. 
In the given string find the index with maximum number of equal characters. 
Example: For string “abbaabbaad”, At index 3 there are 4 equal characters. (Solution 
will be s.substring(idx-length+1, idx+length)). 
 
4. Logical Question: 
How do you measure 4 Litres of water using a 3 Litre and a 5 Litre bucket? 
He asked me to show my logic on the text editor. 
My solution: 
The two numbers in each step represents the amount of water in 3L bucket and 
5L bucket. 
 
0 0 
 
Initially we have empty buckets 
0 5 
 
Poured 5 litres in 5L bucket 
3 2 
 
Poured 3 litres into 3L bucket from 5L bucket 
0 2 
 
Removed 3 litres from 3L bucket 
2 0  
 
Poured 2 litres into 3L bucket from 5L bucket 
2 5 
 
Poured 5 litres into 5L bucket 
3 4 
 
Poured 1 litre from 5L bucket to 3L bucket 
 
We have 4 litres in 5L bucket. 
 
 
 
The interviewer asked me to use the other bucket first. 
 
0 0 
 
Initially we have empty buckets 
 
3 0 
 
Poured 3 litres in 3L bucket 
 
0 3 
 
Poured 3 litres in 5L bucket from 3L bucket 
 
3 3 
 
Poured 3 litres in 3L bucket 
 
1 5 
 
Poured 2 litres in 5L bucket from 3L bucket 
 
1 0 
 
Removed 5 litres from 5L bucket 
 
0 1 
 
Poured 1 litre from 3L bucket to 5L bucket 
 
3 1 
 
Poured 3 litres in 3L bucket. 
 
0 4 
 
Poured 3 litres in 5L bucket. 
We have 4 litres in 5L bucket.

The interview was almost 40 mins long. In the end he asked me if I had any 
questions for him. 
 
Technical Round 2: 
The interview started with my introduction. She asked me about my round 1 
interview experience. Then she asked me to describe the challenges that I faced in 
my recent project and how I overcame them.  
  
Questions I was asked – 
1. Data Structures 
 What is a data structure? 
 What is a hash map data structure? 
 What is stack data structure? 
 Which data structure would you use for LRU cache? (Queue implemented 
using doubly linked lists and hash maps to quickly locate the nodes in the 
linked list). 
2. OOP 
 What are the pillars of OOP?  Give example for each. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/four-main-object-oriented-programming-concepts-of-
java/ 
 What is difference between Object Oriented Programming and Procedural 
Programming. 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/differences-between-procedural-and-object-oriented-
programming/ 
 
 
The interviewer asked me few questions on Java language which I use for 
programming. 
 What is a reference in Java? 
 What is JRE, JDK, JVM? 
 
The interview was almost 30 mins long. In the end, the interviewer asked me if I had 
any questions for her. 
 
HR Round: 
The interview was only for 10 min, on MS Teams. She asked me for my introduction.  
Then she asked me about my location preferences. She finally asked me if I had any 
questions for her.

General Tips: 
 Don’t be nervous. It’s okay if you don’t know everything. They are looking for 
your approach for the problems. 
 Understand the Question Before Answering. When the interviewer asks a 
question, it is ok to ask the interviewer for clarification or to repeat the 
question. You want to know what the interviewer is looking for before you go 
ahead and assume that you have the right answer.  
 Practice HR questions and research well about the company. 
 You can prepare for the coding questions from  
o https://leetcode.com/ 
o https://practice.geeksforgeeks.org/ 
 
 
 
 
 
ALL THE BEST!  স
